# Treeview

A hierarchical list, such as folders and files, where branches expand and collapse and one node at a time is selected. Reach for it when the structure itself is what the user navigates; for a flat list, use a native list or a [table](Table.md).

## Usage

```html
<r-treeview id="files"></r-treeview>
```

```typescript
import type { TreeNode, Treeview } from '@relax.js/components';

interface FileData { id: number; kind: 'folder' | 'file' }

const tree = document.getElementById('files') as Treeview<FileData>;
tree.nodes = [
    {
        label: 'Documents',
        data: { id: 1, kind: 'folder' },
        expanded: true,
        children: [{ label: 'Report.pdf', data: { id: 2, kind: 'file' } }],
    },
    { label: 'Notes.txt', data: { id: 3, kind: 'file' } },
];

tree.addEventListener('r-node-navigated', (event) => {
    const data = event.node.data as FileData;
    openFile(data.id);
});
```

- Clicking the arrow of a branch, or double-clicking its row, expands or collapses it. Clicking a node's label selects it.
- `data` is yours: the tree never reads or changes it, and never changes the node objects you pass in.

### A Navigator

An explorer or outline gives each node a `key`, shows more than a label, loads branches when they open, and sets `nodes` again after every refresh without losing where the user was:

```typescript
const tree = document.getElementById('explorer') as Treeview<FileData>;
tree.setAttribute('label', 'Explorer');
tree.loadChildren = async (node, signal) => {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/folders/${node.key}`, { signal });
    return toNodes(await response.json());
};
tree.nodes = [
    { key: 'src', label: 'src', data: srcFolder, icon: 'folder', hasChildren: true },
    {
        key: 'src/risky.ts', label: 'risky.ts', data: riskyFile, icon: 'file',
        note: '420 lines, long', badge: { text: 'low', tone: 'danger' }, tone: 'danger',
    },
];

// Reflect the file the app just opened, without the tree opening it again.
tree.select('src/risky.ts', { silent: true });

// Remember what the user opens.
tree.addEventListener('r-node-toggled', (event) => saveOpen(event.node.key!, event.expanded));
```

- **Keys** keep expanded branches and the selection across a `nodes` set: a keyed branch keeps whether it was open, a keyed node that was selected stays selected without an event, and a node new to the tree follows its own `expanded`. Without keys, setting `nodes` starts from each node's flags and clears the selection.
- **Lazy branches:** a node with `hasChildren` and no `children` is drawn as a collapsed branch. The first time it is expanded, the tree calls `loadChildren(node, signal)` and marks the node `aria-busy` until the children are shown. A load that fails is reported and the branch collapses, to load again on the next expand. Children that turn out to be none make the node a leaf. Setting `nodes` again aborts loads still running. A branch marked `expanded` loads when drawn.

### Nodes in Markup

A `template` named `data` holding a JSON list of nodes draws them without code:

```html
<r-treeview>
    <template name="data">
        [{ "label": "Root", "data": { "id": 1 }, "children": [{ "label": "Child", "data": { "id": 2 } }] }]
    </template>
</r-treeview>
```

JSON that does not parse reports an error and the tree renders empty.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `label` | `string` | The tree's accessible name |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `nodes` | `TreeNode<T>[]` | The top-level nodes. Setting them redraws the tree; keyed nodes keep their expansion and selection, the rest start from their own flags. Nodes set before the tree connects are drawn when it does. |
| `selected` | `TreeNode<T> \| undefined` (read only) | The selected node |
| `loadChildren` | `(node: TreeNode<T>, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<TreeNode<T>[]>` | Loads the children of a `hasChildren` branch the first time it is expanded. Expanding one without a loader reports an error and the branch stays collapsed. |

```typescript
interface TreeNode<T = unknown> {
    label: string;
    data: T;
    key?: string;          // identifies the node across nodes sets; select, expand and collapse take it
    children?: TreeNode<T>[];
    expanded?: boolean;    // shows the children when the node is first drawn
    hasChildren?: boolean; // a branch whose children loadChildren supplies
    icon?: string;         // an icon name before the label
    note?: string;         // secondary text after the label, shown as given
    badge?: TreeNodeBadge; // after the note
    tone?: Tone;           // colours the icon and label; without an icon, shows the tone's icon
}

interface TreeNodeBadge {
    text?: string;  // shown as given
    count?: number; // written for the locale; zero is shown
    tone?: Tone;
}
```

A key used by more than one node reports an error and reaches the first. A node tone that is not one of the five reports an error and the node is untoned.

## Methods

Every method taking a node takes the node object or its `key`, and throws an error naming the tree when the node is not in it. Pass a node from `nodes`, `add()` or `find()`, or a key the tree holds.

### find(match, under?): TreeNode\<T\>[]

Returns the nodes whose `data` matches, in display order. Pass `under` to search only that node's descendants.

```typescript
const files = tree.find((data) => data.kind === 'file');
const inDocuments = tree.find((data) => data.kind === 'file', files[0]);
```

### select(node, options?)

Selects a node, expands every branch above it and dispatches `r-node-navigated`. With `{ silent: true }` it dispatches nothing, for reflecting a selection the app made itself, such as the file it just opened.

```typescript
const [report] = tree.find((data) => data.id === 2);
tree.select(report);
tree.select('src/app.ts', { silent: true });
```

### add(node, parent?)

Adds a node as the last top-level node, or as the last child of `parent`. A leaf that gets a child becomes a collapsed branch.

```typescript
tree.add({ label: 'Draft.docx', data: { id: 4, kind: 'file' } }, documents);
```

### expand(node): Promise\<void\> and collapse(node)

Show or hide a branch's children. `expand` resolves once the children are shown, loading them first for a `hasChildren` branch, and rejects when that load fails. Neither selects anything or dispatches an event.

```typescript
await tree.expand('src');
tree.select('src/app.ts', { silent: true });
```

## Events

### r-node-navigated

Dispatched as `NodeNavigatedEvent` when a node is selected by a click, the keyboard or `select()` without `silent`. Bubbles.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `node` | `TreeNode` | The selected node |

### r-node-toggled

Dispatched as `NodeToggledEvent` when the user expands or collapses a branch with the arrow, a double-click or the keyboard. `expand()`, `collapse()`, `select()` and a `nodes` set dispatch nothing. Bubbles.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `node` | `TreeNode` | The branch |
| `expanded` | `boolean` | Whether it is now expanded |

## Parts

The tree renders into the light DOM, so style it with ordinary selectors:

| Selector | What it is |
|----------|------------|
| `r-treeview .tree` | The outer list |
| `r-treeview .node` | One node, with `aria-expanded` on branches, `aria-selected`, and `aria-busy` while its children load |
| `r-treeview .node-row` | The row holding a node's arrow, icon, label, note and badge; `data-tone` when the node has a tone |
| `r-treeview .toggle` | The expand/collapse arrow, empty on leaves |
| `r-treeview .icon` | The node's icon |
| `r-treeview .label` | A node's text |
| `r-treeview .note` | The node's secondary text |
| `r-treeview .node-row r-badge` | The node's [badge](../dashboard/Badge.md) |
| `r-treeview .children` | The list of a branch's children |

## Variables

Rows take `--item-padding`, hover `--surface-hover`, the selected node `--surface-selected`, focus `--focus-ring`. A toned node's icon and label take `--tone`, its note `--text-muted`. See [Theming](../../authoring/Theming.md#variables).

## Accessibility

The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: `role="tree"` named by `label`, `treeitem` and `group`, with `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected` and `aria-busy`. One node is in the tab order at a time.

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Down / Up | Next / previous visible node |
| Right | Expands a collapsed branch, or moves to its first child |
| Left | Collapses an expanded branch, or moves to the parent |
| Home / End | First / last visible node |
| Enter / Space | Selects the node |
| A letter or digit | Next visible node whose label starts with what was typed; keys typed in quick succession spell one prefix |
